newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. calls on Iraq to give up arms ambitions.
newsitem.headline: U.N. calls on Iraq to give up arms ambitions.

text.p: Rolf Ekeus, the chief U.N. arms inspector, called on Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's government on Friday to abandon "once and for all" ambitions to retain or acquire weapons of mass destruction.
In a major half-year report to the Security Council, Ekeus said remaining problems in ridding Iraq of dangerous arms and related materials were political rather than technical.

"Their solution requires a major political decision by Iraq's leadership to give up, once and for all, all capabiities and ambitiion to retain or acquire the proscribed weapons," his report concluded.

Specifically, Ekeus said that little remained unknown about Baghdad's nuclear, biological, chemical and ballistic missile potential. But what was unknown could still cause devastating damage and casualities.

He also said Iraq was hindering a long-term monitoring programme to make sure it does not reacquire dangerous arms and some governments were not giving his group data on weapons materials they had sold to Iraq in the past.

A clean bill of health by Ekeus, head of the U.N. Special Commission on ridding Iraq of weapons of mass destruction, is a key requirement before the embargo on Iraqi oil exports can be lifted entirely. Iraq has been under U.N. sanctions since its invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
